note: points: the tick marks (x ticks below the axis, y ticks left of it), each set on its axis line as fitted through the ink. The y axis leans 0.92 deg to the left (4.5 px over its height) and the x axis falls 0.37 deg to the right, a skew of 1.29 deg that the lettering shares; the x ticks close up to the right (73.0, 71.8, 70.5, 70.0, 69.7, 70.0 px per 100 m; the affine fit leaves 1.9 px). The frame convention of Figs 10, 12, 13 and 14 (fig10.py): x is read between the x ticks (xgrid: the tick columns on the x axis line, piecewise linear, extended by one tick step at both ends, the end interval repeated, as a safeguard for a point past the last tick) along lines parallel to the drawn y axis (lean: the fitted axis lines, x axis row = xaxis[0] col + xaxis[1], y axis col = yaxis[0] row + yaxis[1]); y is the affine fit of the points. digitize.py reads xgrid by column alone (it ignores lean), so its overlay of these curves is off by the lean; fig10.py prints the overlay with this mapping.
